g.text: Frame 1. The 80386 ljmp targets the next task's TSS selector
The CPU stores into the old TSS
CR3, EIP, EFLAGS
EAX ECX EDX EBX ESP EBP ESI EDI
ES CS SS DS FS GS
The LDT selector sits in that TSS too
Instructions after ljmp run when switched back
The CPU loads from the new TSS
CR3, EIP, EFLAGS
the same general and segment registers
LDT
Execution resumes at the saved EIP
This is a jump, so NT is not set by it
Frame 2. The other three store the callee-saved registers in their own block
RV32 swtch(old, next). a0 is the old block, a1 the new one
ra, sp, s0-s11. ret goes to the loaded ra
ARMv7 r0 is old, r1 is next. The CPU stays in SVC
r4-r11, lr, sp. bx lr goes to the loaded lr
AArch64 x0 is old, x1 is next. The CPU stays at EL1
x19-x30, sp. ret goes to the loaded x30
